commit.description: Bump version, commit all changes, and push to GitHub
commit.template:
Bump the version by incrementing the MINOR number (MAJOR.MINOR format), create a git tag, stage all changes, commit, push to origin master, AND add a new entry to server/changelog.json with the version, today's date, and the commit description. Steps:
1. Get the LATEST tag: git tag --sort=-version:refname | Select-Object -First 1
2. Parse vMAJOR.MINOR (e.g., v0.21), increment MINOR, form new tag (e.g., v0.22)
3. Analyze the changes with git diff --stat and git diff HEAD to understand what was modified, then AUTO-GENERATE a concise commit message in Spanish summarizing the changes (do NOT ask the user for a message)
4. Read server/changelog.json, prepend a new entry: {"version": "vX.YY", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "description": "<AUTO_GENERATED_MESSAGE>"}, write it back
5. Stage all: git add -A
6. Commit: git commit -m "<AUTO_GENERATED_MESSAGE>"
7. Create the new tag on the new commit: git tag <NEW_VERSION>
8. Push: git push origin master
9. Push tags: git push origin --tags
IMPORTANT: use PowerShell for all git commands. Create the tag AFTER the commit, not before. Add the changelog entry BEFORE staging. You MUST auto-generate the commit message from the actual changes in the repo. Do NOT ask the user for input. Execute all steps and report the new version.
